records: On 30 August 2021, the Security Council adopted resolution 2593 by 13 votes to none, with China and Russia abstaining. France, the United Kingdom and the United States submitted the draft (S/PV.8848, p. 2). The Council condemned the 26 August attacks near Kabul airport (para. 1). It demanded that Afghan territory never be used to threaten or attack other countries or for terrorist shelter, training, planning or financing (para. 2). It called for greater aid and unrestricted, safe humanitarian access and underlined parties’ obligations under international humanitarian law (para. 3). It reaffirmed human rights, including those of women, children and minorities, and encouraged an inclusive negotiated settlement with full, equal and meaningful participation by women (para. 4). It noted the Taliban’s travel commitment and expected safe, orderly departures. It called for stronger airport security and requested efforts for rapid, secure reopening (paras. 5–6).
